previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with a history of cocaine-induced cardiomyopathy, insulin-dependent diabetes, COPD, and chronic hepatitis C was admitted for acute on chronic systolic heart failure exacerbation, triggered by poor adherence to fluid and sodium restrictions. He presented with weight gain, leg edema, and shortness of breath. Treatment included IV furosemide for diuresis, which successfully reduced his weight from 92.3 kg to 83.7 kg, improved respiratory symptoms, and resolved pulmonary edema. His kidney function improved from a creatinine of 2.2 to 1.8, and losartan was restarted and titrated to 25 mg daily. Insulin therapy was adjusted due to labile glucose levels, and he was discharged on glargine 30 units at bedtime. He was counseled on daily weight monitoring, low-salt diet, fluid restriction, and avoidance of cocaine and tobacco, with follow-up arranged.

# Chronic, decompensated systolic CHF: The patient as a baseline 
LVEF ___, NYHA III-IV, baseline orthopnea, and last ECHO was 
___. He was found to be ___ lbs above dry weight and developed 
new pulmonary edema. He was started on lasix gtt @ 10mg/hr after 
80mg IV lasix bolus with a goal of -1L. As Losartan was held due 
to ___, his blood pressure was controlled with hydralazine 10mg 
TID. A beta blocker could not be used given his h/o active 
cocaine use. He was continued on home ASA 81 mg, digoxin 0.0625 
mg daily, pravastatin 40 mg daily. Daily Digoxin levels were 
obtained in the setting of ___, which were felt to be 
therapeutic for the indication of heart failure. He was 
transitioned to 12.5mg PO lorsartan and hydralazine was 
discontinued. He was transitioned from lasix drip to home 
torsemide 200mg daily with the addition of once weekly 
metolazone. He should take metolazone once a week on Wednedays 
before being seen in clinic to evaluate his volume status and 
weight. His weight on discharge was 82.4 kg.

# Elevated Troponin: The pt presented with a troponin elevation 
to 0.07, which increased to 0.09 and 0.11. Cardiology was 
consulted who noted that his troponins had been elevated 
previously in this range, likely due to his underlying 
cardiomyopathy combined with CKD. His troponins then bean to 
downtrend to 0.08. He was continued on ASA and pravastatin.

# Right-sided chest pain: On presentation, there was initial 
concern for acute PE, however, D-dimer was negative. Wih 
downtrending trops, the pain was also not likely cardiac 
ischemia. His UTox was negative for cocaine. With some 
reproducibility on exam, the most likely etiology is MSK pain in 
the setting of cough. He was continued on acetaminophen for pain 
and his pain resolved by discharge. 

# ___ on CKD IIIb: The pt's baseline Cr appears to be 1.6-2.0. 
Small changes in his Cr were difficult to interpret due to 
non-linearity of eGFR to Cr relationship in this range. His 
creatinine peaked at 2.5 and improved with diuresis. His 
creatinine was back to 2.0 on discharge. Electrolytes were 
monitored in the setting of diuresis as well and repleted as 
necessary.
